desc:
Every subset of nums (chosen by position, so there are exactly 2n of them, the empty subset included) has a sum; the empty subset has sum 0.

Return the sums of all 2n subsets in non-decreasing order. If several subsets have the same sum, that sum appears once for each of them.
hints: Think about how the list of all subset sums of the first i elements grows when you look at element i + 1.
Each old subset can either leave the new element out (same sum) or take it (sum plus the element).
Start with [0]. For every element x, replace the list by the old list followed by the old list with x added to every entry. Sort at the end.
editorial: Let S be the list of sums of all subsets of the elements processed so far, initially [0] for the empty subset. A new element x doubles the number of subsets: the old ones without x keep their sums, the old ones with x added have sums increased by x. So the new list is S + [s + x for s in S]. After all elements, sort the list.

The same list falls out of a backtracking search with an include/skip choice per element that records the running sum at the leaves. The doubling loop avoids recursion and performs 2<sup>n</sup> additions in total; sorting dominates with O(n · 2<sup>n</sup>).
